messages:
Jun: hi all, new hire here. trying to get local services running. docker-compose brings up postgres + redis but my app complains it can't connect to redis: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379. i'm on macbook m1, using Docker Desktop. i'm not sure if the app should talk to 127.0.0.1 or the compose network. any tips?
Olga: welcome Jun! :wave: your app running on host (not in a container) would need to use localhost with port mapping, but if your app runs in a container it should use the service name (e.g., `redis:6379`). how are you starting the web app? `docker-compose up` or `npm start` locally?
Jun: running node server locally (not containerized) while postgres+redis are in compose. compose has ports set for both. i can `redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6379 ping` and it times out. weird. compose snippet below:
```
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:6-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pass
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```
Chris: do you have another redis instance on the host? `lsof -i :6379` or `sudo lsof -nP -iTCP:6379 -sTCP:LISTEN` to see. Also check Docker Desktop networking settings and make sure port forwarding allowed.
Jun: `lsof` shows nothing listening. docker ps shows redis container up. docker logs show `Ready to accept connections`. but host cannot connect. tried `curl http://localhost:6379` (dumb) and `redis-cli -h localhost -p 6379 ping` -> connection refused.
Olga: could be the socket binding inside the container only listening on IPv6 or unix socket? try `docker exec -it $(docker ps -qf "name=redis") redis-cli ping` to verify internal. If that works, then port mapping might be blocked by macOS firewall or Docker Desktop edge setting.
Jun: internal exec ping works -> PONG. i checked firewall, nothing obvious. i also noticed Docker Desktop had "Use the new virtualization framework" turned on; toggled it off and restarted and host can connect now. odd.
Chris: yep we've seen that on some macOS versions where the new framework causes port forwarding flakiness. fallback is run the app in a container or use `host.docker.internal` as the host from inside containers. since you're running node on host, host should be able to reach mapped ports normally; toggling the setting is the quick fix.
Jun: thanks! one more q: postgres bind mount i tried as a host dir but kept hitting permission errors (initdb could not create directory). what's our recommended compose for mac devs?
DevEx: recommended snippet in README: use named volume for postgres and set a short healthcheck so your scripts wait for readiness. example we add to onboarding README:
```
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL","pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  pgdata:
```
DevEx: also run `./dev/wait-for-services.sh` before running `npm test` — the script polls health endpoints and runs migrations.
Jun: followed that and all green now. added a note to my onboarding checklist. thanks everyone :tada:
